name: isp1362_urb_enqueue
prose: Slice cut the head: isp1362_urb_enqueue(hcd, urb, mem_flags) (isp1362-hcd.c:1216-1395). Precondition: urb is a valid URB; the function takes isp1362_hcd->lock itself (irqsave). Postcondition: it returns -ENOSPC at once for an isochronous pipe. If the endpoint (hep->hcpriv) does not exist it allocates an isp1362_ep with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure, returned before the lock). Under the lock it returns -ENODEV (freeing the new ep) if neither root port has USB_PORT_STAT_ENABLE or the HC is not running, and the error of usb_hcd_link_urb_to_ep (freeing the new ep) if linking fails. Otherwise it initialises the new ep (or reuses hep->hcpriv) and stores it in hep->hcpriv, numbers the request, puts a control or bulk endpoint on the async schedule if it is not already scheduled, and for an interrupt endpoint without a branch calls balance(); if balance returns a negative value the function unlinks the URB from the endpoint (usb_hcd_unlink_urb_from_ep) and returns that value, and the newly allocated ep is not freed: it stays in hep->hcpriv. Otherwise the branch is recorded, the endpoint is added to the periodic schedule and the load updated. On success urb->hcpriv = hep, the matching start_atl_transfers or start_intl_transfers runs and it returns 0. The lock is released on each return after it was taken.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): after balance() fails hep->hcpriv = ep was already set (1306) and the ep is not freed (1328-1331, 1385-1387); old prose said any freshly allocated endpoint is freed on every failure path

name: cvmx_usb_poll_channel
prose: Slice cut the head: cvmx_usb_poll_channel(usb, channel) (octeon-hcd.c:2595-2920). Precondition: usb is an initialised octeon_hcd and channel is a valid host channel number. Postcondition: returns 0 after the steps below. It reads HCINT for the channel. With CVMX_USB_INITIALIZE_FLAGS_NO_DMA: if HCCHAR has both chena and chdis set it writes HCCHAR back unchanged (CN31XX workaround) and returns; if the channel has not halted (chhltd clear) and chena is set it writes HCINTMSK with only the channel-halted mask, sets chdis in HCCHAR and returns; if not halted, chena clear and xfercompl clear it logs "interrupt without halt" and returns without writing. In DMA mode it returns at once if chhltd is clear. Otherwise it writes HCINTMSK = 0 and sets the channel's bit in usb->idle_hardware_channels; if usb->pipe_for_channel[channel] is NULL it returns (the mask and idle bit have already been changed). With a pipe it detaches the pipe from the channel, clears CVMX_USB_PIPE_FLAGS_SCHEDULED, computes the bytes transferred from HCTSIZ/HCCHAR (zero for setup stages), adds them to transaction->actual_bytes, sets pipe->pid_toggle from HCTSIZ.pid and sets NEED_PING for a high-speed bulk OUT pipe. A negative byte count completes the transaction with CVMX_USB_STATUS_ERROR. Otherwise by the first set HCINT bit: stall (pid_toggle = 0, complete with STALL), xacterr, bblerr, datatglerr (complete with the matching error), nyet (non-split: retries = 0 and complete with OK if no buffer space is left or the last packet was short; split: retries++, and every fourth retry rewinds to the start-split stage), ack (retries = 0, NEED_PING cleared, then the control, bulk, interrupt or isochronous transfer handler), nak (clears active_split if it is this transaction, retries = 0, stage rewound, next_tx_frame advanced) and otherwise it reads the port status: enabled port gives retries++, a disabled port completes with CVMX_USB_STATUS_ERROR.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the CN31XX path writes HCCHAR, the non-DMA running path writes HCINTMSK and HCCHAR, and the no-pipe path has already masked interrupts and marked the channel idle (2624-2648, 2670-2677); old prose said 'untouched'

name: io_watchdog_func
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is io_watchdog_func(t) (ohci-hcd.c:747-873), the timer callback of ohci->io_watchdog; the name ohci_io_watchdog does not exist. Precondition: t is the io_watchdog timer of a valid ohci_hcd; no lock is held by the caller. Postcondition: returns nothing. It takes ohci->lock (irqsave) and releases it on each return. If the interrupt status has no WDH bit and wdh_cnt equals prev_wdh_cnt, then with a nonzero prev_donehead it goes to the "died" path (usb_hc_died, ohci_dump, _ohci_shutdown, the timer is not rearmed), and with prev_donehead zero it only sets takeback_all_pending. Otherwise it walks ohci->eds_in_use: for an ED with a pending_td, if takeback_all_pending or OKAY_TO_TAKEBACK holds, the pending TD is added to the done list; then it finds the last TD the controller has passed and, when that TD changed, sets ed->takeback_wdh_cnt = wdh_cnt + 2 and ed->pending_td to it. It then calls ohci_work. If rh_state is OHCI_RH_RUNNING and the frame counter equals prev_frame_no while at least one root-hub port is enabled and not suspended it also takes the "died" path; otherwise, if eds_in_use is not empty, it remembers the current frame number, stores wdh_cnt and the donehead register in prev_wdh_cnt and prev_donehead and rearms the timer with IO_WATCHDOG_DELAY. At the end ohci->prev_frame_no is set to the remembered frame number, which is IO_WATCHDOG_OFF whenever the timer was not rearmed (including the died paths).
note: slice cut head; real name io_watchdog_func; prose rechecked against the code: the died path from the first test skips ohci_work, the second one runs after it

name: ohci_rh_suspend
prose: ohci_rh_suspend(ohci, autostop) (ohci-hub.c:47-141); the parameter autostop is distinct from the field ohci->autostop. It is called with ohci->lock held (it drops and retakes it). Postcondition: it reads the control register into ohci->hc_control. If the HCFS state is OHCI_USB_RESUME it writes OHCI_USB_RESET to the control register (and reads it back) and returns -EBUSY; if it is OHCI_USB_RESET it returns -EBUSY; in both cases rh_state, ohci->autostop and next_statechange are not changed. If it is OHCI_USB_SUSPEND and the field ohci->autostop is 0 it returns 0 without any register write ("already suspended"); if the field is nonzero it continues. Otherwise: if the parameter autostop is 0 and any schedule-enable bits are set it clears them, writes and reads back the control register, writes OHCI_INTR_SF to intrstatus, sets ohci->autostop = 0, releases the lock, sleeps 8 ms and retakes the lock. It then runs update_done_list and ohci_work, disables the SF interrupt, with OHCI_QUIRK_GLOBAL_SUSPEND suspends every enabled unsuspended port, sets OHCI_CTRL_RWE when the root hub has remote wakeup enabled or the parameter autostop is set (otherwise it disables the RHSC and RD interrupts and clears RWE), writes OHCI_USB_SUSPEND to the control register and reads it back. Only when the parameter autostop is 0 does it then set next_statechange (5 ms), ohci->autostop = 0 and rh_state = OHCI_RH_SUSPENDED. It returns 0 on these paths and the lock is held on return.
note: reviewer R1 point (already-suspended and autostop paths return 0 without setting rh_state) was already stated in the prose, so that claim was not a defect; prose rewritten to separate the parameter autostop from the field ohci->autostop

name: ohci_rh_resume
prose: ohci_rh_resume(ohci) (ohci-hub.c:152-302), called with ohci->lock held (it drops and retakes it). Postcondition: it saves ohci->autostop in a local (autostopped), sets ohci->autostop = 0 and reads the control register into hc_control. If OHCI_CTRL_IR or OHCI_SCHED_ENABLES is set: with rh_state not OHCI_RH_RUNNING the status is -EBUSY (BIOS/SMM active), with rh_state RUNNING it is a duplicate resume and the function returns 0 without writes. Otherwise by the HCFS state: SUSPEND writes OHCI_USB_RESUME (schedule enables cleared) and reads back; RESUME only logs; OPER and any other value (RESET, lost power) give -EBUSY. For -EBUSY, if autostopped was 0 it drops the lock, calls ohci_restart (its result becomes the return value), calls usb_root_hub_lost_power and retakes the lock; if autostopped was nonzero it returns -EBUSY without restarting. If not autostopped it drops the lock, sleeps 33 ms, rereads HCFS and, if it is not OHCI_USB_RESUME, logs, retakes the lock and returns -EBUSY; otherwise it zeroes the schedule head/current registers, writes the HCCA address and calls periodic_reinit. In both the autostopped and the normal case it enables OHCI_INTR_INIT (and OHCI_INTR_SF if ed_rm_list is non-empty), writes OHCI_USB_OPER and reads back, sleeps 3 ms (not autostopped), writes OHCI_CONTROL_INIT|OHCI_USB_OPER keeping the RWC bit, and for the non-autostopped case sleeps 10 ms and retakes the lock (the autostopped case keeps the lock throughout). It then sets next_statechange, restarts the control and bulk schedules (head registers and enable bits) when ed_rm_list is empty and their tails exist, enables the periodic and isochronous lists when bandwidth requests exist, sets rh_state = OHCI_RH_RUNNING and returns 0 with the lock held.
note: prose verified branch by branch against 152-302; R2 claims (ohci_restart result returned, EBUSY without restart for autostopped) were already in the prose

name: ohci_hub_status_data
prose: Slice cut the head: ohci_hub_status_data(hcd, buf) (ohci-hub.c:468-532). Precondition: buf is writable for 1 byte, or 2 bytes when ohci->num_ports > 7; the caller does not hold ohci->lock. Postcondition: it takes ohci->lock (irqsave) and releases it before returning. It returns 0 with buf untouched if the hardware is not accessible or if the AMD756 bogus-NDP erratum is detected. Otherwise buf[0] is set to 1 if the root hub status has LPSC or OCIC and to 0 otherwise (buf[1] = 0 when num_ports > 7, which also makes the length 2); the RHSC bit in intrstatus is cleared and read back; for each port whose status has CSC, PESC, PSSC, OCIC or PRSC the matching bit is set (bit i+1 of buf[0] for i < 7, bit i-7 of buf[1] otherwise) and changed is set; HCD_FLAG_POLL_RH is set or cleared according to ohci_root_hub_state_changes. It returns the length (1, or 2 when num_ports > 7) if any change was found (hub or port) and 0 otherwise.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): buf[0] is set to 1 on LPSC/OCIC, not always initialised to 0 (490-493); old prose contradicted itself

name: end_unlink_async
prose: Slice cut the head: end_unlink_async(oxu) (oxu210hp-hcd.c:2058-2095). Precondition: oxu->lock is held and oxu->reclaim is the QH whose unlink from the hardware async list has finished. Postcondition: returns nothing. It cancels TIMER_IAA_WATCHDOG, sets the reclaim QH to QH_STATE_IDLE with qh_next cleared and drops the reclaim reference (qh_put). It then sets oxu->reclaim to the QH's chained reclaim QH (next), clears oxu->reclaim_ready and the QH's own reclaim pointer and calls qh_completions(oxu, qh) (which may drop and retake the lock). If qh->qtd_list is not empty and the HC is running it calls qh_link_async, which links the QH back into the async list and sets QH_STATE_LINKED without taking a new reference (the async-list reference is kept); otherwise it drops the async-list reference with qh_put and, if the HC is running and the async list head has no next QH, arms TIMER_ASYNC_OFF. Finally, if there was a chained QH (next), oxu->reclaim is set to NULL and start_unlink_async(oxu, next) is called, which makes next the new oxu->reclaim unless it is the async list head (then oxu->reclaim stays NULL).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): qh_link_async takes no reference (oxu210hp-hcd.c:1892-1928); the async-list reference simply stays when the QH is relinked; old prose said a new refcount is taken

name: oxu_hub_control
prose: Slice cut the head: oxu_hub_control(hcd, typeReq, wValue, wIndex, buf, wLength) (oxu210hp-hcd.c:3540-3829). Precondition: the caller does not hold oxu->lock (taken here with spin_lock_irqsave); buf is writable for 4 bytes (GetHubStatus, GetPortStatus) or a hub descriptor (GetHubDescriptor). Postcondition: returns 0 or -EPIPE (stall); the lock is released on each return. ClearHubFeature and SetHubFeature only accept C_HUB_LOCAL_POWER and C_HUB_OVER_CURRENT, write nothing and return 0; other selectors give -EPIPE. GetHubDescriptor fills the descriptor, GetHubStatus writes four zero bytes. ClearPortFeature (port index 1..ports, else -EPIPE) clears or acknowledges ENABLE, C_ENABLE, SUSPEND (starts a 20 ms resume; -EPIPE if reset is active or the port is suspended but not enabled), POWER (only if the controller has port power control), C_CONNECTION, C_OVER_CURRENT in the port status register (C_SUSPEND and C_RESET write nothing) followed by a read of the command register; other selectors give -EPIPE. GetPortStatus (valid port, else -EPIPE) builds the 32-bit status/change word from the port register and stores it little-endian in buf; it may start or complete a resume (arming the root-hub timer, clearing reset_done and writing the port register; a failed 2 ms handshake gives -EPIPE) and a reset completion (750 us handshake, check_reset_complete; failure gives -EPIPE) and hands the port to the companion controller (sets PORT_OWNER) when a connected port is in companion_ports. SetPortFeature (port index masked to 8 bits; the test selector is the high byte) returns 0 without touching the port if PORT_OWNER is set; otherwise SUSPEND (-EPIPE if not enabled or in reset), POWER, RESET (-EPIPE during resume; sets PORT_RESET, clears enable, reset_done = jiffies + 50 ms) and TEST (selector 1..5 else -EPIPE; ehci_quiesce, ehci_halt and the test mode written) update the port register followed by a command-register read; other selectors give -EPIPE. Any other typeReq gives -EPIPE.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the hub-feature requests only validate the selector and write no register (3560-3569, 3747-3756); old prose said they update the port status register

name: uhci_result_common
prose: Slice cut the head: uhci_result_common(uhci, urb) (uhci-q.c:1170-1249). Precondition: urb->hcpriv is a valid urb_priv with its qh and td_list. Postcondition: it walks the TDs of urbp->td_list in order. If a TD is still active it returns -EINPROGRESS at once; TDs processed earlier in the same call have already been counted in urb->actual_length, removed from the list and moved through qh->post_td, so the queue is not untouched. For each completed TD it adds the actual length to urb->actual_length. A TD with an error status gives ret = uhci_map_status(...) (a negative errno). A TD without error status but with a short packet gives, for a control queue, ret = 1 if it is not the last data TD; for bulk or interrupt, -EREMOTEIO if URB_SHORT_NOT_OK is set, else ret = 1 if it is not the URB's last TD. Each processed TD is removed from the list, the previous qh->post_td is freed and the TD becomes qh->post_td. When ret becomes nonzero the walk stops: a negative ret sets qh->element to the terminator, qh->is_stopped = 1, qh->needs_fixup for non-control queues and qh->initial_toggle = the TD's toggle (inverted for -EREMOTEIO) and returns ret; ret = 1 returns the result of uhci_fixup_short_transfer, which is -EINPROGRESS for a control queue and 0 for bulk/interrupt. If all TDs complete without a stop, it returns 0. The function does not return 1.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): an active TD found after earlier TDs already updated actual_length, were removed and became post_td (1178-1233); old prose said the queue is untouched

name: renesas_setup_rom
prose: Slice cut the head: renesas_setup_rom(pdev, fw) (xhci-pci-renesas.c:427-546). Precondition: pdev is a PCI device; fw->data is readable for fw->size bytes (only the first 4*(fw->size/4) bytes are used as 32-bit words). Postcondition: it returns true only if all of these steps pass: the magic word is written to RENESAS_DATA0, external ROM access is enabled in ROM_STATUS, the result bits (6:4) read back as 0, every one of the fw->size/4 words is downloaded with renesas_fw_download_image, DATA0/DATA1 busy bits (ROM_STATUS_MSB bits 0 and 1) clear within RENESAS_RETRY polls, 0 is written to ROM_STATUS (bypass removal), the ROM result field reads RENESAS_ROM_STATUS_SUCCESS within RENESAS_RETRY polls, the RELOAD bit is written, and the RELOAD bit clears within RENESAS_RETRY polls. It returns false otherwise, as a plain boolean. Failures of the external-access write, the result read, nonzero result bits, a download step, the DATA0/1 status read and the DATA0/1 wait first write 0 to ROM_STATUS (result ignored) and then return false; failures of the magic-word write, the bypass-removal write, the final result loop (read error or timeout), the RELOAD write and the RELOAD wait return false without that extra write.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the RELOAD write and wait are present (516-539), as the old prose said; prose otherwise rechecked against the remove_bypass labels

name: handle_cmd_completion
prose: Slice cut the head: handle_cmd_completion(xhci, event) (xhci-ring.c:1810-1948). Precondition: xhci has an initialised command ring and event is a command completion event TRB; cmd_list is non-empty whenever the event matches the ring dequeue TRB. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns without completing a command, without cancelling the command timer and without advancing the dequeue if slot_id >= MAX_HC_SLOTS (warning); if the completion code is COMP_COMMAND_RING_STOPPED it first calls complete_all(&xhci->cmd_ring_stop_completion) and returns; if the event's cmd_trb DMA is not the DMA address of the ring dequeue TRB (or that address is 0) it warns and returns. After those checks it takes the first command in cmd_list and cancels xhci->cmd_timer; if the command's command_trb is not the ring dequeue pointer it logs an error and returns (the timer stays cancelled). If the completion code is COMP_COMMAND_ABORTED it sets cmd_ring_state = CMD_RING_STATE_STOPPED, and if the command's recorded status is also COMP_COMMAND_ABORTED it clears xhci->current_cmd if it was this command and jumps straight to the completion step below. Otherwise it runs the per-type handler (enable slot, disable slot, address device, set dequeue, reset endpoint, reset device with the slot id taken from the command TRB, NEC firmware; config endpoint and stop endpoint only if the command has no completion; evaluate context and get bandwidth do nothing; a no-op command whose recorded status is COMP_COMMAND_RING_STOPPED changes the completion code to COMP_COMMAND_RING_STOPPED; unknown types are only logged). Then, before the command is completed, if cmd_list has more than one entry the next command becomes xhci->current_cmd and xhci_mod_cmd_timer re-arms the timer, else xhci->current_cmd is cleared if it was this command. Finally (also on the aborted shortcut) xhci_complete_del_and_free_cmd completes, removes and frees the command with the final completion code and inc_deq advances the command ring dequeue.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the timer re-arm / next current_cmd selection (1936-1942) comes before xhci_complete_del_and_free_cmd and inc_deq (1945-1947); old prose said after

name: xhci_urb_dequeue
prose: Slice cut the head: xhci_urb_dequeue(hcd, urb, status) (xhci.c:1763-1894). Precondition: the caller does not hold xhci->lock; urb was submitted to this HCD. Postcondition: it takes xhci->lock (irqsave) and releases it on each return. It returns the nonzero result of usb_hcd_check_unlink_urb if the URB was already unlinked or completed. It takes the err_giveback path (urb private data freed, URB unlinked from its endpoint, lock released, URB given back with -ESHUTDOWN, function returns 0) if the virtual device or the URB private data is missing, the endpoint or its ring is missing, the URB's first TD is no longer on the endpoint ring (its cancelled-list entries are removed), or the HC is XHCI_STATE_HALTED (its TDs are taken off the lists); no TD is marked cancelled on these paths. If the status register reads all ones or the HC is dying it calls xhci_hc_died and returns 0. Otherwise it marks every unfinished TD of the URB TD_DIRTY and appends it to the endpoint's cancelled list unless it is already there, and then: if the endpoint state has EP_STOP_CMD_PENDING, EP_HALTED or SET_DEQ_PENDING it queues nothing and returns 0; if it has EP_CLEARING_TT it processes the cancelled TDs at once and returns 0; otherwise it allocates a command with GFP_ATOMIC (failure: -ENOMEM, with the TDs already marked) and queues a Stop Endpoint command, sets EP_STOP_CMD_PENDING and rings the command doorbell and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): on the early -ESHUTDOWN giveback paths no TDs are marked for cancellation (1787-1797, 1811-1834, 1887-1893); old prose grouped them with 'successfully marked'

name: xhci_hcd_init
prose: xhci_hcd_init (xhci.c:5691-5718), a module init function with no parameters. Postcondition: it contains compile-time BUILD_BUG_ON size checks of the register and context structures; it returns -ENODEV if usb_disabled(); otherwise it calls xhci_debugfs_create_root() and xhci_dbc_init() and returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: contract dropped: the function touches global debugfs and DbC state; prose rechecked

name: isp1760_hub_control
prose: Slice cut the head: isp1760_hub_control(hcd, typeReq, wValue, wIndex, buf, wLength) (isp1760-hcd.c:2193-2446). Precondition: buf is writable for 4 bytes (GetHubStatus, GetPortStatus) or a hub descriptor; the function takes priv->lock itself (irqsave) and releases it before returning. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EPIPE. -EPIPE is returned for an unknown typeReq, an invalid hub or port feature selector, a port index of 0 or above the port count, a port state that forbids the operation (suspend while in reset or not enabled, reset during resume, clear-suspend in reset or while suspended but not enabled), and also when the 2 ms wait for PORT_RESUME to clear or the 750 us wait for PORT_RESET to clear in GetPortStatus fails. ClearHubFeature and SetHubFeature accept only C_HUB_LOCAL_POWER and C_HUB_OVER_CURRENT and do nothing. ClearPortFeature performs ENABLE (clears PORT_PE), SUSPEND (starts resume signalling and sets reset_done), POWER (when port power control exists), C_CONNECTION (writes PORT_CSC to acknowledge it, which sets the bit in the register image as the code does), C_ENABLE, C_SUSPEND, C_OVER_CURRENT and C_RESET (no action) and then reads CMD_RUN. GetHubDescriptor fills buf; GetHubStatus writes four zero bytes; GetPortStatus builds the status/change word (it may start or finish resume and reset handling) and stores it little-endian in buf. SetPortFeature does nothing and returns 0 if PORT_OWNER is set; otherwise ENABLE, SUSPEND, POWER and RESET (which, for a connected, not-enabled port in low-speed line state, hands the port to the companion controller by setting PORT_OWNER, and otherwise sets PORT_RESET, clears PORT_PE and sets reset_done 50 ms ahead).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the clear-and-wait failures in GetPortStatus go to 'error' and return -EPIPE (2318-2325, 2339-2345); R1 C_CONNECTION point is described above

name: test_ctrl_queue
prose: Slice cut the head: test_ctrl_queue(dev, param) (usbtest.c:1201-1416). Precondition: dev and param are valid. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP at once if param->sglen == 0 or param->iterations > UINT_MAX / param->sglen. It returns -ENOMEM if kcalloc of the urb array fails (nothing else done) or, after cleanup, if allocating any urb (simple_alloc_urb, which allocates its transfer buffer too) or its setup packet fails. The subcase number is i % NUM_SUBCASES (16), so the default case returning -EINVAL is unreachable. It then submits all urbs with usb_submit_urb(GFP_ATOMIC): a failed submission stores that errno in the context status and stops submitting. It waits for the queue to drain if anything was submitted. ctrl_complete counts completions, resubmits urbs while more are needed, accepts the statuses expected for each subcase, and records in the context status only the first unexpected status of a completed urb (for example a negative urb status such as -EPIPE, -EREMOTEIO or -ETIMEDOUT, or -EDOM for out-of-order completion), after which it unlinks the pending urbs; failures of its own resubmission or unlink calls are only logged. All urbs, their setup packets and the array are freed and the context status is returned: 0 when every submitted urb completed acceptably, otherwise the submit errno or the first recorded status (the context status starts as -ENOMEM and is only reached with that value if an allocation failed).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the transfer-buffer allocation inside simple_alloc_urb is another -ENOMEM source (1369-1371); R2 point (resubmit errors are only logged) is in the prose, the initial usb_submit_urb errno is returned (1389-1395, 1415)

name: yurex_write
prose: Slice cut the head: yurex_write(file, user_buffer, count, ppos) (yurex.c:426-522). Precondition: file->private_data is a live usb_yurex; user_buffer is readable for min(count, 16) bytes. Postcondition: n = min(count, 16). If n == 0 it returns 0 without taking dev->io_mutex. Otherwise it takes dev->io_mutex interruptibly (failure: -EINTR); with the mutex held it returns -ENODEV if dev->disconnected, -EFAULT if copy_from_user fails and -EINVAL if the first byte is not a recognised command, each after unlocking. It then fills dev->cntl_buffer (padding, plus the command bytes or a decoded number), submits dev->cntl_urb (GFP_ATOMIC) and, if the submission did not fail, waits up to YUREX_WRITE_TIMEOUT; it then kills the urb and unlocks the mutex. It returns the negative errno of a failed usb_submit_urb; otherwise, for a numeric set command that was acknowledged before the timeout (timeout nonzero) it stores the parsed value in dev->bbu under dev->lock (spin_lock_irq); it returns n if the wait did not time out and -EIO if it timed out.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): dev->bbu is assigned between spin_lock_irq and spin_unlock_irq (513-517); old prose also omitted that the store only happens when the wait did not time out; R1's -ETIMEDOUT is not in the code (timeout gives -EIO)

name: musb_g_reset
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is musb_g_reset(musb) (musb_gadget.c:2032-2099); the name musb_start does not exist. Precondition: musb is a valid MUSB device; musb->lock is held on entry (the function may drop and retake it). Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads DEVCTL. If there is a gadget driver and the gadget speed is not USB_SPEED_UNKNOWN it drops musb->lock, calls usb_gadget_udc_reset and retakes the lock; otherwise, if DEVCTL has the host-request bit, it writes MUSB_DEVCTL_SESSION to DEVCTL. It then reads POWER and sets musb->g.speed to USB_SPEED_HIGH if HSMODE is set and USB_SPEED_FULL otherwise, sets is_active = 1, is_suspended = 0 (MUSB_DEV_MODE), address = 0, ep0_state = MUSB_EP0_STAGE_SETUP, clears may_wakeup, g.b_hnp_enable, g.a_alt_hnp_support and g.a_hnp_support and sets g.quirk_zlp_not_supp = 1. If the gadget is not OTG, or DEVCTL has MUSB_DEVCTL_BDEVICE, the OTG state becomes OTG_STATE_B_PERIPHERAL with is_a_peripheral 0; otherwise OTG_STATE_A_PERIPHERAL with is_a_peripheral 1. Finally it calls musb_gadget_vbus_draw(&musb->g, 8) and ignores the result.
note: slice cut head; real name musb_g_reset; old prose omitted the usb_gadget_udc_reset/HR branch and the fact that a non-OTG gadget is always put in B_PERIPHERAL

name: musb_g_ep0_halt
prose: Slice cut the head: musb_g_ep0_halt(e, value) (musb_gadget_ep0.c:990-1048). Precondition: e is a usb_ep of a MUSB controller (ep0). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL at once if e is NULL or value is 0. Otherwise it takes musb->lock (irqsave) and returns -EBUSY if ep->req_list is not empty. It selects endpoint 0 and takes csr = musb->ackpend; for ep0_state MUSB_EP0_STAGE_TX, ACKWAIT or RX it re-reads CSR0 into csr first; for these and for STATUSIN and STATUSOUT it sets MUSB_CSR0_P_SENDSTALL in csr, writes CSR0, sets ep0_state = MUSB_EP0_STAGE_IDLE, sets ackpend = 0 and returns 0. For any other ep0_state it logs, changes nothing and returns -EINVAL. The lock is released on each return after it was taken.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): for TX/ACKWAIT/RX the code falls through to the shared tail that sets ep0_state = IDLE and ackpend = 0 (1023-1039); R1's value==0 claim is covered by the -EINVAL return for value 0

name: usbhsf_fifo_select
prose: Slice cut the head: usbhsf_fifo_select(pipe, fifo, write) (renesas_usbhs/fifo.c:316-352). Precondition: pipe and fifo are valid; fifo belongs to pipe's controller. Postcondition: it returns -EBUSY at once, without writing fifo->sel or selecting the pipe, if usbhs_pipe_is_busy(pipe) or usbhsf_fifo_is_busy(fifo). Otherwise base = the pipe number; for the DCP pipe, bit 5 (ISEL) is added when write == 1, and in host mode usbhs_dcp_dir_for_host(pipe, write) is called. It writes base | MBW_32 to fifo->sel and then reads fifo->sel up to 1024 times with a 10 us delay between reads; if (value & ((1 << 5) | 0xF)) equals base it calls usbhs_pipe_select_fifo(pipe, fifo) and returns 0. After 1024 failed reads it logs "fifo select error" and returns -EIO without selecting the pipe; fifo->sel keeps the last value written. No locks are taken.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): busy at entry is handled, returning -EBUSY (326-328), so 'requires not busy' was wrong; contract dropped

name: usbhsg_recip_handler_std_set_device
prose: usbhsg_recip_handler_std_set_device(priv, uep, ctrl) (mod_gadget.c:260-276). Precondition: priv, uep and ctrl are valid; ctrl is the raw setup packet (the function converts wValue and wIndex with le16_to_cpu itself). Postcondition: it calls usbhsg_recip_handler_std_control_done(priv, uep, ctrl) in every case. If wValue equals USB_DEVICE_TEST_MODE it first does that call, then waits 100 us and calls usbhs_sys_set_test_mode(priv, wIndex >> 8); any other wValue only does the control-done call. It returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the conversion is done here (264, 268), so it is not a precondition that the caller converted; prose otherwise matched

name: cyberjack_read_int_callback
prose: Slice cut the head: cyberjack_read_int_callback(urb) (cyberjack.c:248-302). Precondition: urb->context is a usb_serial_port with cyberjack private data. Postcondition: returns nothing. If urb->status is nonzero it returns at once without resubmitting anything. Otherwise, if urb->actual_length is 4 and data[0] is 0x01, it computes size = (data[3] << 8) + data[2] + 3 and, under priv->lock, reads old_rdtodo; if old_rdtodo > SHRT_MAX - size it releases the lock and skips to the resubmit step, otherwise it adds size to priv->rdtodo, releases the lock and, if old_rdtodo was zero, submits port->read_urb (GFP_ATOMIC; an error is logged). In all of these cases (status zero) it finally resubmits port->interrupt_in_urb (GFP_ATOMIC), logging an error if that fails. priv->lock is not held on return.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): a nonzero urb->status returns immediately without resubmitting the interrupt urb (258-260); old prose said it always resubmits first

name: ftdi_232am_baud_base_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_232am_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, base) returns an unsigned short. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 1073741823 (so 2 * baud fits an int), base >= 0 and base + baud <= INT_MAX (the rounding adds baud to base). Postcondition: let d = DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(base, 2 * baud), which for these non-negative values is (base + baud) / (2 * baud); if (d & 7) == 7 then d is increased by 1; let q = d >> 3 truncated to 16 bits and f = d & 7. The result is q | 0xc000 if f == 1, q | 0x4000 if f >= 4, q | 0x8000 if f is 2 or 3, and for f == 0 it is q, except that q == 1 gives 0. No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: ftdi_232am_baud_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_232am_baud_to_divisor(baud) returns an unsigned short: the value of ftdi_232am_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, 48000000), with the same arithmetic. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 1073741823 (then base + baud = 48000000 + baud cannot overflow an int). No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: ftdi_232bm_baud_base_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_232bm_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, base) returns a u32. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 1073741823, base >= 0 and base + baud <= INT_MAX. Postcondition: let d = DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(base, 2 * baud) = (base + baud) / (2 * baud); q = d >> 3, f = d & 7, frac = {0, 3, 2, 4, 1, 5, 6, 7}[f]; v = q | (frac << 14) (q is not masked, so a large q overlaps the fraction bits). The result is 0 if v == 1, 1 if v == 0x4001, and v otherwise. No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: ftdi_232bm_baud_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_232bm_baud_to_divisor(baud) returns a u32: the value of ftdi_232bm_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, 48000000), with the same arithmetic. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 1073741823. No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: ftdi_2232h_baud_base_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_2232h_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, base) returns a u32. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 214748364 (10 * baud fits an int), base >= 0 and base <= 268435455 (8 * base fits an int), and 8 * base + 5 * baud <= INT_MAX (the rounding adds 5 * baud). Postcondition: let d = DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(8 * base, 10 * baud) = (8 * base + 5 * baud) / (10 * baud); q = d >> 3, f = d & 7, frac = {0, 3, 2, 4, 1, 5, 6, 7}[f]; v = q | (frac << 14); v becomes 0 if it is 1 and 1 if it is 0x4001; the result is v | 0x00020000. No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: ftdi_2232h_baud_to_divisor
prose: ftdi_2232h_baud_to_divisor(baud) returns a u32: the value of ftdi_2232h_baud_base_to_divisor(baud, 120000000), with the same arithmetic. Precondition: baud > 0 and baud <= 214748364 (then 8 * 120000000 + 5 * baud fits an int). No state is read or written.
note: rechecked against ftdi_sio.c:1125-1198; overflow limits of DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST added; contract left empty (helper-dependent)

name: alauda_write_lba
prose: Slice cut the head: alauda_write_lba(us, lba, page, pages, ptr, blockbuffer) (alauda.c:810-911). Precondition: us->extra media info and zone maps are valid; ptr holds pages * pagesize bytes; blockbuffer holds blocksize * (pagesize + 64) bytes; page + pages <= blocksize. Postcondition: it calls alauda_ensure_map_for_zone (result ignored) and reads pba = lba_to_pba[zone][lba_offset]. If pba == 1 it prints a warning and returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_GOOD without touching the media or the maps. If alauda_find_unused_pba finds no free block it returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR. Otherwise it reads the old block into blockbuffer with alauda_read_block_raw (a result other than USB_STOR_XFER_GOOD is returned, no map changed) or, if pba is UNDEF, zeroes blockbuffer. It writes the LBA tag into every page's control area, checking the two ECCs of each page and replacing them if they do not match, copies the new pages into blockbuffer with freshly computed ECCs, and writes the block to new_pba with alauda_write_block (a failure is returned, no map changed). Then it sets pba_to_lba[zone][new_pba - zone*zonesize] = lba (the LBA, not the PBA) and lba_to_pba[zone][lba_offset] = new_pba. If pba was not UNDEF it erases the old block with alauda_erase_block; a failure is returned with the maps already updated and the old block's pba_to_lba entry not set to UNDEF; on success that entry is set to UNDEF. It returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_GOOD on success.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): pba_to_lba[zone][new_pba_offset] receives lba (898); old prose said the new PBA, and also said ECCs are always recomputed for the old contents (they are only repaired when mismatched)

name: sddr09_read_map
prose: Slice cut the head: sddr09_read_map(us) (sddr09.c:1197-1397). Precondition: us->extra is an sddr09_card_info whose lba_to_pba and pba_to_lba are NULL or kmalloc'ed arrays (they are freed here). Postcondition: it returns -1 at once, touching nothing, if info->capacity is 0. Otherwise it allocates a control buffer (at most 64 KB, a multiple of the control size) and frees the old tables; allocation failure of the buffer or the new tables returns -1 through the cleanup label, and so does a failing sddr09_read_control (whatever its own code was). On any such failure after the capacity test both tables are freed and set to NULL. On success it fills the tables with kmalloc_array(numblocks, sizeof(int)): blocks 0 and 1, blocks with an all-zero control field, blocks with a malformed or bad-parity or out-of-range LBA field and duplicate LBAs become UNUSABLE (or are erased with sddr09_erase and marked UNDEF when erase_bad_lba_entries is set); unwritten blocks stay UNDEF; valid ones set pba_to_lba and lba_to_pba; per 1024-block zone blocks beyond 1000 usable ones are marked SPARE; info->lbact is the number of LBAs found and the function returns 0. The control buffer is freed on each return after it was allocated.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): every failure path sets result = -1 (1226, 1240, 1263), so -ENOMEM or the read error code are not returned; old prose said tables are freed on all failures, but the capacity==0 return happens first and touches nothing

name: usb_stor_Bulk_transport
prose: Slice cut the head: usb_stor_Bulk_transport(srb, us) (transport.c:1111-1343). Precondition: srb is a SCSI command with valid cmnd and cmd_len; us has an iobuf large enough for a CBW and a CSW and its bulk pipes set up. Postcondition: it increments us->tag, builds the CBW (32 bytes with iobuf[31] zeroed under US_FL_BULK32, else US_BULK_CB_WRAP_LEN) and sends it; a result other than USB_STOR_XFER_GOOD returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR. With US_FL_GO_SLOW it sleeps 125-150 us. If scsi_bufflen(srb) is nonzero it runs the data stage: USB_STOR_XFER_ERROR returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR, USB_STOR_XFER_LONG sets fake_sense, and a short data-in whose transferred length is exactly US_BULK_CS_WRAP_LEN and whose bytes carry US_BULK_CS_SIGN is treated as a skipped data phase (the CSW is taken from the transfer buffer, that buffer region is zeroed and the residue is set to transfer_length). Otherwise it reads the CSW, retrying once after a zero-length short read and once more after a stall; if the result is still not USB_STOR_XFER_GOOD it returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR. It returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR if the CSW tag differs from us->tag (unless US_FL_BULK_IGNORE_TAG), if Status exceeds US_BULK_STAT_PHASE, or if the signature differs from a previously learned us->bcs_signature (the first CSW signature seen is stored). If the CSW residue is nonzero and US_FL_IGNORE_RESIDUE is clear it either sets US_FL_IGNORE_RESIDUE (status OK, no residue recorded so far, INQUIRY of 36 bytes or READ_CAPACITY of 8 bytes) or sets the scsi residue to max(current residue, min(csw residue, transfer_length)). Finally status OK returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_NO_SENSE after copying usb_stor_sense_invalidCDB into srb->sense_buffer if fake_sense is set, else USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_GOOD; US_BULK_STAT_FAIL returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_FAILED; US_BULK_STAT_PHASE returns USB_STOR_TRANSPORT_ERROR.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the code does set the residue to max(current, min(residue, transfer_length)) (1310-1311); R1's fake_sense point is right and was already in the prose (only XFER_LONG sets it)

name: uas_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: uas_probe(intf, id) (uas.c:1002-1068). Precondition: intf is the interface being probed and id its device id. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV, before allocating anything, if uas_use_uas_driver says the device is not to be handled or if uas_switch_interface fails. It allocates the Scsi_Host with scsi_host_alloc (failure: -ENOMEM after setting alternate setting 0 with usb_set_interface), fills in the host and uas_dev_info (including the anchors, lock and work items) and calls uas_configure_endpoints (failure: the error is returned after alternate setting 0 is restored and the host is put, without freeing streams and before the interface data is set). It then sets can_queue = qdepth - 2, stores shost in the interface data and calls scsi_add_host: on failure it frees the streams, clears the interface data, restores alternate setting 0, puts the host and returns the error. On success it schedules scan_work and returns 0; the registered host stays until disconnect.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): scsi_host_alloc failure goes to set_alt0 (1018-1019, 1063-1064) so alternate setting 0 is restored; the old prose was right

name: usb_stor_control_thread
prose: Slice cut the head: usb_stor_control_thread(__us) (storage/usb.c:380-515), the body of the control kthread. Precondition: __us is a valid us_data with its mutex, completions, flags and proto_handler set up for the life of the thread. Postcondition: it loops waiting interruptibly on us->cmnd_ready; if the wait is interrupted it leaves the loop. On each wakeup it takes us->dev_mutex and the host lock; if us->srb is NULL it releases both and leaves the loop. If US_FLIDX_TIMED_OUT is already set it sets srb->result to DID_ABORT << 16 and skips the command. Otherwise it drops the host lock and, in this order: for DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL sets DID_ERROR << 16; else for a nonzero target without US_FL_SCM_MULT_TARG or a LUN above max_lun sets DID_BAD_TARGET << 16; else for INQUIRY with US_FL_FIX_INQUIRY fills a fake response and sets SAM_STAT_GOOD; else calls us->proto_handler(srb, us) and usb_mark_last_busy. It retakes the host lock; if srb->result is DID_ABORT << 16 it forgets the command (srb = NULL, so scsi_done_direct is not called); if US_FLIDX_TIMED_OUT is set it completes us->notify and clears US_FLIDX_ABORTING and US_FLIDX_TIMED_OUT; it sets us->srb = NULL, releases the host lock and dev_mutex and, if srb is still set, calls scsi_done_direct(srb). After the loop is left it waits until kthread_should_stop() and returns 0.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the second loop (506-513) tests kthread_should_stop() and the function returns 0 (514); R2's TIMED_OUT/DID_ABORT points were already as described

name: dp_altmode_probe
prose: dp_altmode_probe(alt) as defined in displayport.h (lines 5-6): the fallback definition compiled only when CONFIG_TYPEC_DP_ALTMODE is not enabled (otherwise the header only declares it). In that configuration it ignores alt and returns -ENOTSUPP (-524). It takes no locks and has no side effects.
note: reviewer R1 RIGHT: the old prose said 'always'; this body exists only in the !CONFIG_TYPEC_DP_ALTMODE branch, the enabled configuration uses a different implementation declared here; function-like stub with a non-static definition in the header

name: dp_altmode_remove
prose: dp_altmode_remove(alt) as defined in displayport.h (line 7): the fallback definition compiled only when CONFIG_TYPEC_DP_ALTMODE is not enabled (otherwise the header only declares it). In that configuration it ignores alt, does nothing and returns nothing. It takes no locks.
note: reviewer R1 RIGHT: describes only the !CONFIG_TYPEC_DP_ALTMODE stub, so the prose now says so explicitly

name: wcd939x_usbss_set
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is wcd939x_usbss_set(usbss) (wcd939x-usbss.c:240-532), which programs the USB sub-system switch from the fields usbss->mode, usbss->svid and usbss->orientation (reverse is orientation == TYPEC_ORIENTATION_REVERSE); it has no mode or orientation parameter. Precondition: usbss has an initialised regmap. Postcondition: it first selects the target: USB if mode is below TYPEC_STATE_MODAL or (svid is 0 and mode is USB2 or USB3); with an svid, DP only for DP states C and E and USB plus DP for states D and F; audio if svid is 0 and mode is TYPEC_MODE_AUDIO; anything else returns -EOPNOTSUPP before any register is written. It then, returning the regmap error on failure, clears all switch enables, clears the switch selects, sets the OVP bias bits for MG1 and MG2 and clears the equalizer enable; it writes the audio FSM trigger without checking the result and sleeps. For audio it sets the AATC mode, selects the DNL/DPR, sense/mic and AGND switches by orientation, adjusts the MG bias, enables those switches, writes the FSM delays, triggers the FSM (errors returned) and applies the linearizer coefficients (errors ignored) and returns 0. Otherwise it sets the USB mode; for USB it enables the equalizer unless mode is TYPEC_STATE_SAFE and selects and enables the DN/DP switches; for DP it sets the leakage canceller and threshold, selects the AUX switches by orientation and enables the AUX-to-MGX switches (the result of that last write is not checked) after which it sleeps; it returns 0. A failed register write in a checked step leaves the earlier writes in place.
note: slice cut head; real function wcd939x_usbss_set; old prose assumed mode and orientation parameters and claimed all failures are reported, but the FSM-trigger, the final AUX enable and the coefficient writes are unchecked and unsupported modes return -EOPNOTSUPP first

name: qcom_pmic_typec_port_set_cc
prose: Slice cut the head: qcom_pmic_typec_port_set_cc(tcpc, cc) (qcom_pmic_typec_port.c:458-524). Precondition: tcpc belongs to a valid pmic_typec port; the function takes the port spinlock itself (irqsave) and releases it before returning. Postcondition: it reads TYPEC_MISC_STATUS_REG (a failure is returned). For cc TYPEC_CC_OPEN or RP_DEF it chooses the 80 uA source current, for RP_1_5 180 uA, for RP_3_0 330 uA (all in EN_SRC_ONLY mode) and for TYPEC_CC_RD the 80 uA value with EN_SNK_ONLY; any other cc returns -EINVAL (with a warning) before anything is stored. In EN_SRC_ONLY mode it writes the value to TYPEC_CURRSRC_CFG_REG (a failure is returned with cc not stored); in EN_SNK_ONLY mode nothing is written. It then stores cc in pmic_typec_port->cc, calls qcom_pmic_set_cc_debounce (sets debouncing_cc and schedules the 2 ms debounce work) and returns 0. On the error returns no debounce work is scheduled and cc is not stored.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): this code has no -EBUSY return and no TYPEC_MODE_CFG_REG write (469-524); prose verified; slice cut head

name: vdm_run_state_machine
prose: Slice cut the head: vdm_run_state_machine(port) (tcpm.c:2593-2780), called with port->lock held (by the VDM work). Postcondition: returns nothing; it acts on port->vdm_state: READY: if the port is not attached the state becomes ERR_BUSY. If port->state is none of SRC_READY, SNK_READY, SRC_VDM_IDENTITY_REQUEST it only sets vdm_sm_running = false and the state stays READY. For a structured VDM initiator header it calls tcpm_ams_start for the command (DISCOVER_IDENT, DISCOVER_SVID, DISCOVER_MODES, ENTER_MODE, EXIT_MODE, ATTENTION, vendor commands; other commands give -EOPNOTSUPP); for DISCOVER_IDENT success it clears send_discover_prime (SOP') or send_discover; for -EAGAIN it zeroes vdo_data[0] and schedules the discover retry; any negative result sets the state to ERR_BUSY and returns. Otherwise it sets SEND_MESSAGE and schedules the VDM work with delay PD_T_SINK_TX for a structured initiator from a source at PD 3.0 or later, else 0. WAIT_RSP_BUSY: vdo_data[0] = vdo_retry, vdo_count = 1, state READY, tcpm_ams_finish. BUSY: state ERR_TMOUT; tcpm_ams_finish if an AMS is active. ERR_SEND: if port->state is SRC_VDM_IDENTITY_REQUEST: tcpm_ams_finish, state DONE and the port state set to SRC_SEND_CAPABILITIES. Else if vdm_retries < 3: vdm_retries++, state READY, and tcpm_ams_finish for a structured initiator. Else tcpm_ams_finish; if tx_sop_type is TCPC_TX_SOP the state stays ERR_SEND; otherwise for DISCOVER_IDENT it zeroes vdo_data[0] and queues a Discover SVID on SOP with tcpm_queue_vdm, which sets the state to READY; for DISCOVER_SVID or DISCOVER_MODES it calls tcpm_register_partner_altmodes (the state stays ERR_SEND); other commands change nothing. SEND_MESSAGE: builds the VDM message (SOP' uses the prime revision and message id) and calls tcpm_pd_transmit: a negative result sets ERR_SEND; otherwise vdm_retries = 0, vdo_data[0] = 0, state BUSY and the VDM work is scheduled with vdm_ready_timeout. Any other state (IDLE, UNDEFINED, DONE, ERR_BUSY, ERR_TMOUT) is left unchanged.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): after the SOP' Discover Identity fallback tcpm_queue_vdm sets VDM_STATE_READY (1623), so the old 'stays ERR_SEND' was wrong; R2's retries-exhausted case is described per tx_sop_type above

name: tcpm_src_attach
prose: Slice cut the head: tcpm_src_attach(port) (tcpm.c:4438-4500). Precondition: port is a valid tcpm_port. Postcondition: it returns 0 at once, changing nothing, if port->attached is already true. Otherwise polarity is CC2 if port->cc2 is TYPEC_CC_RD, else CC1. It calls tcpm_set_polarity (a negative result is returned), then tcpm_enable_auto_vbus_discharge(port, true), then enables VCONN with tcpm_set_vconn(true) only if the CC pin not used for polarity reads TYPEC_CC_RA (a failure is returned with nothing undone, the auto discharge stays enabled). Then tcpm_set_vbus(true): on failure VCONN is switched off and the error returned; tcpm_set_roles(true, TYPEC_STATE_USB, TYPEC_SOURCE, source data role): on failure VBUS and then VCONN are switched off and the error returned; if port->pd_supported, set_pd_rx(true): on failure the mux is set to TYPEC_STATE_SAFE with USB_ROLE_NONE and no orientation, then VBUS and VCONN are switched off and the error returned. On success it sets pd_capable = false, partner = NULL, attached = true, send_discover = true, send_discover_prime = false and returns 0. On error returns the port stays not attached; the polarity and the auto vbus discharge setting are not undone.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): on failure the code undoes the earlier-enabled steps (VBUS/VCONN/mux) and the old prose called them 'later steps'; auto vbus discharge is enabled right after polarity and never undone

name: tps6598x_interrupt
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is tps6598x_interrupt(irq, data) (tipd/core.c:985-1048), the irq_handler of the tps6598x variant; the name tps6598x_irq_handler does not exist. Precondition: data is a valid struct tps6598x whose tps->lock is not held by the caller. Postcondition: it takes tps->lock and releases it on each return. It reads the version register (an error is only warned about) and uses it to choose the event length, then reads INT_EVENT1 into event1[2] (this read is performed twice in the code, the first result is overwritten) and INT_EVENT2 into event2[2]; a failed read goes to the unlock exit with the event words as they are. If all four u64 words (event1[0], event1[1], event2[0], event2[1]) are zero it goes to the unlock exit. Otherwise it writes the event words back to INT_CLEAR1 and INT_CLEAR2 (write errors ignored), reads the status (a failure goes to the exit), reads the power status if the POWER_STATUS_UPDATE bit is set (failure goes to the exit), reads the data status via data->read_data_status if DATA_STATUS_UPDATE is set (failure goes to the exit) and calls tps6598x_handle_plug_event if PLUG_EVENT is set. After unlocking it returns IRQ_HANDLED if any of the four event words is nonzero, else IRQ_NONE (so a failed event read that leaves the words zero also gives IRQ_NONE).
note: slice cut head; real name tps6598x_interrupt; old prose said 'four event bytes'; they are four u64 words, and the version read and double event1 read were not mentioned

name: tps25750_start_patch_burst_mode
prose: Slice cut the head: tps25750_start_patch_burst_mode(tps) (tipd/core.c:1423-1483). Precondition: tps is valid; its device node should have "firmware-name" and "reg-names"/"reg" entries for "patch-address". Postcondition: it calls tps_request_firmware (error returned; that helper itself releases the blob and returns -EINVAL for an empty firmware, and a failed request leaves no blob). With the blob held it looks up "patch-address" in "reg-names" and reads the matching "reg" cell (errors returned), returns -EINVAL for an address of 0 or in 0x20..0x23, fills the PBMs data (address, firmware size, TPS_BUNDLE_TIMEOUT) and runs tps25750_exec_pbms (its error returned; -EINVAL for an invalid bundle size or slave address and -ETIMEDOUT for an invalid-timeout result from the controller). It then calls tps25750_write_firmware, which temporarily switches the I2C client address to the patch address and the adapter timeout to 5 s and writes the first firmware byte as the register address and the remaining fw->size - 1 bytes as data with regmap_raw_write (error returned), then waits 500 us and returns 0. Once the blob was obtained it is released with release_firmware on each return before returning.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): right that the empty-firmware blob is released inside tps_request_firmware and that the data write is fw->size-1 bytes after the first byte used as register address (1345-1348, 1372); the old prose's overall return/release statement matched
